title: Pharmacokinetics, Efficacy and Safety of infliximab CT-P13 Subcutaneous as Induction Therapy in Patients with Active Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis. The « PASSPORT-2 Trial »
official: Pharmacokinetics, Efficacy and Safety of infliximab CT-P13 Subcutaneous as Induction Therapy in Patients with Active Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis. The « PASSPORT-2 Trial »
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate that induction treatment with CT-P13 SC is non-inferior to CT-P13 IV in terms of pharmacokinetics at Week 6.
conditions: Immune Bowel Disease (Crohn's disease and Ulcerative colitis)

interventions.name: Remsima 100 mg powder for concentrate for solution for infusion
Remsima 120 mg solution for injection in pre-filled syringe
Remsima 120 mg solution for injection in pre-filled pen

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Male or female aged between 18 and 75 years old.
2. Diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease according to the ECCO criteria for at least 3 months: ●	Moderately to severely active CD defined as 8 ≤ HBI ≤ 16 OR ●	Moderately to severely active UC defined as 5 ≤ partial Mayo score ≤ 9
3. Patient had received conventional therapy for active UC (corticosteroids alone or in combination with thiopurines and 5-aminosalicylates) or CD (corticosteroids and/or immunomodulators) but had not responded despite an adequate course of therapy.
4. Patient with at least one objective sign of disease activity on biology, endoscopy or imaging.  •	For patients with CD, objective signs of activity may include endoscopic ulcerations, cross-sectional imaging showing active inflammation, or elevated fecal calprotectin.  •	For patients with UC, objective signs of activity may include endoscopic Mayo subscore ≥ 2 or equivalent findings.
5. Patient who will start infliximab CT-P13 as part of standard of care.
6. Patient who has received full information about the organization of the research, who consent to his or her participation and to the use of his or her data.
7. Patient affiliated to or beneficiary of a social security plan.
8. ► Inclusion criteria for Women of Childbearing Age:  Women of childbearing age should consider the use of appropriate contraception to prevent pregnancy and continue its use for at least 6 months after the last CT-P13 treatment. Women should choose one of the following methods of contraception:  •	Combined hormonal contraception containing oestrogen and progesterone (oral, IUD, transdermal, injectable) combined with ovulation inhibition initiated at least 30 days before Baseline (Week 0).  •	Progestin-only hormonal contraception (oral, injectable, implantable) associated with ovulation inhibition initiated at least 30 days before the first injection of CT-P13.  •	Bilateral tubal occlusion (can be performed by hysteroscopy, provided that hysterosalpingography confirms the success of the procedure).  •	Intrauterine device (IUD).  •	Practicing true abstinence, defined as: abstaining from heterosexual intercourse when this corresponds to the subject's preferred and usual lifestyle (periodic abstinence [e.g. calendar method, ovulation method, hypothermal method, post-ovulation methods] and withdrawal are not acceptable).  ► Inclusion Criteria for Women Not of Childbearing Age:  Women do not need to use contraception during or after treatment with study drug if they are considered not of childbearing age due to one of the following situations:  •	Premenopausal women with permanent infertility following hysterectomy, bilateral salpingectomy or bilateral oophorectomy.  •	Postmenopausal women. •	Age > 55 years without menstruation for 12 months or more without alternative medical cause.  •	Age ≤ 55 years without menstruation for 12 months or more without alternative medical cause AND a folliculostimulin (FSH) level > 30 IU/L.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Combination therapy with an immunomodulator.
2. Patient for whom the clinician considers a high short-term (≤ 3 months) risk of surgical intervention.
3. Patient who has received thiopurine or methotrexate within 4 weeks before inclusion visit.
4. Patients with CD with predominant ano-perineal lesions, where fistula management is the main indication for infliximab CT-P13.
5. Hypersensitivity to the active substance, to other murine proteins or to any of the excipients listed in the summary of product characteristics (SmPC) of infliximab CT-P13
6. Patients with tuberculosis or other severe infections such as sepsis, abscesses and opportunistic infections
7. Patient who had infection requiring oral antibiotics within 2 weeks or parenteral injection of antibiotics within 4 weeks prior to the first administration of the study drug, other serious infection within 6 months prior to the first administration of study drug or recurrent herpes zoster or other chronic or recurrent infection within 6 weeks prior to the first administration of the study drug.
8. Patient for whom no pre-anti-TNF testing was performed.
9. Patients with moderate or severe heart failure (NYHA class III/IV).
10. Pregnant woman or breastfeeding woman
11. Adult person under legal protection (any form of public guardianship)
12. Previous treatment with infliximab.
13. Acute severe UC.
14. Foreseeable risk of imminent hospitalization (as assessed by the investigator).
